question: Tumour lysis syndrome in ALL is characterised by hyperkalaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hypocalcaemia, and hyperuricaemia, and is prevented by aggressive IV hydration and allopurinol before initiating chemotherapy.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. TLS is defined by the metabolic tetrad: hyperkalaemia + hyperphosphataemia + hypocalcaemia + hyperuricaemia, following rapid tumour cell lysis. Prevention requires hydration and allopurinol/rasburicase before induction chemotherapy in high-risk ALL.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. TLS occurs when rapid cell death releases intracellular contents: potassium (hyperkalaemia), phosphate (hyperphosphataemia → secondary hypocalcaemia from calcium-phosphate binding), and nucleic acids → uric acid (hyperuricaemia → acute urate nephropathy). Prevention: aggressive IV hydration (2–4× maintenance), allopurinol (or rasburicase in high-risk cases), and monitoring electrolytes.
